- Predicting future dynamics in computer vision
- Early methods: convolutional encoders + recurrent predictors or GANs, with brittle pixel-level representations and error accumulation

- Object-based predictors improve short-term accuracy but face challenges: occlusions, large numbers of interacting entities, compounding errors in extended simulations

The text to evaluate (final paragraph):

- Contrasts LfD (Learning from Dynamics) and LfI (Learning from Intuition)
- Shows LfI classifier attains comparable/better performance than SOTA LfD on PHYRE
- Uses ground-truth dynamics as oracle to establish upper bound
- Replaces oracle with predicted dynamics, observes approximation errors degrade performance
- Extensive experiments across LfI architectures show intuition-based approaches are simpler and more robust
